utterances.text: I never actually met the man, but I do know that he was -- was he the president of SAO Krajina or something like that? And as such, he came up to Manjaca, but I wasn't present when he arrived, or at least I can't remember having been. He promised in talking to them to boost morale, the prisoners morale. He promised that they would be released, some 90 per cent, or what did he say, 70 per cent of them would be released. And he faced us with a problem, the security organs that we were for the camp, because there was general unrest, whereas he failed to keep his promise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And indeed you say:

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we need to redact -- sorry, can we go back, lines 23 to 25 of page 62. Part of it anyhow. I'm told if I repeat the words it has to be redacted as well, so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So would Your Honours order that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May that then document, please, be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P498 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't need that one, it's already exhibit. And yes, could you have a brief look, please, at document 517 on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We saw earlier your complaint that the people from Omarska had arrive without anything to show why they were there. Was this Simo Drljaca from Prijedor security station forwarding to the commander the lists plus allegedly the documentation that went with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: You can see that from this letter to the camp commander that he is sending some documents attached to the letter, but he doesn't say how many notes or whatever. Yes, notes did arrive subsequently after the people had already arrived, but.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just very quickly, please, if we have a look at the third page in English, and in B/C/S, it's for prisoner number 52, it's, I think, the third page in B/C/S as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We see there, I think an example of something you had been complaining about, number 52, the gentleman there was born in 1926, so he was clearly over 60.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be -- it's on our 65 ter list, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P499 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at document number 1282. Can we just go into private session very quickly, Your Honour, on this one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, we are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- 2436. Again, please, not to go out on the screen. And to be marked under seal. This is a report. If we look at the last page -- it's the third page, sorry, in each. No, second page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you just say, sir, that's the gentleman who you referred to earlier; is that right? Can you just say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you made aware of the contents of this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Upon arrival, yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we look at the second page, please, in B/C/S then, and it's the -- I think it's still -- the second page in English and also the second page, sorry, in B/C/S. The bottom part, please, of the English, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The -- it records that representatives of the CSB Banja Luka visited, is that right, the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And besides all the [indiscernible] taking of the prisoners according to the established criteria, the most critical CSBs turned a deaf ear to the orders that they received.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P501 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we look, please -- this is not on our 65 ter list -- 10233. Just to note the contents really, because you dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the order, is it not, in fact, if we looked at the second page we'd see it was signed on behalf of General Talic for the construction of the church for the repair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, can we just have that marked for identification if we think it's necessary to add it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P502 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just checking on the remainder of the documents, if I may, very quickly, to see if I can -- I appreciate I've taken a little more time. Yes, well, Your Honours, this document obviously will in fact come in through another witness, so again I'm going to skip that. That was 2423. Your Honours, there's a daily -- there's a report which, can I perhaps just get him to identify it and then leave it at that. Could I have up, please, 24 -- 2579, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If one looks at the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, the second page in each. I'm so sorry. It's a November report. No, the first page is fine. Then again, can this not go out on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, is this the same gentleman you referred to earlier who actually wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And by November of 1992, had preparations started to release people from the camp and move them to another camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes, that was the beginning of November. For the 14th of November, the first group was supposed to go, so we were preparing for their departure to third countries.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be then admitted and marked, and then could I have up 2349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 2579 will be Exhibit P503.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Under seal, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you so much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The final document is dated the 9th of November, what number is it, 2349. Again, please, not on the screen and under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think this one is your report, and you describe here that prisoners who have arrived from the prison in Banja Luka have been physically abused and are wearing visible injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because we haven't got enough time, I'm not going to go through the rest of the report. Your Honours, again can that be admitted and marked under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P504 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to show, however, the witness a couple of clips from videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, sir, were you present at Manjaca when Paddy Ashdown, Lord Ashdown arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I was, but I do know that the visit did take place, but I just can't remember whether I was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. In fact, I tell you what, that's already an exhibit, so we'll skip that one. Can we come to one where it's not because there's just something I want to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 2330. This is, Your Honour, the last topic, I think. It's in sanction. There is no sound, there should be sound. All right, I don't know what has happened to sound but it may not matter. First of all, can we pause it there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Behind the reporter, we can see people standing there with their heads bowed. First of all, who were those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: They were prisoners. I know one of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you identify which one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Vahid Ceric, the first from the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They are all standing with their heads bowed down like that. Was that an order that they were to stand like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes, that was the order, generally. Work in the camp and law and order in the camp was that the prisoners should move around with their heads down and hands behind their backs. I suppose to be less capable of putting up any resistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, although there is sound, I don't think I need for these purposes trouble you. May I simply ask that it be marked and admitted for this. In fact, can we -- as we move on one bit further, I think we are going to see the prisoner a bit more that you are talking about. Can we just fast forward it slightly. I don't know why there's no sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, is that -- that's the person you are talking about, Vahid Ceric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes, that's Vahid Ceric.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, may I ask that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P505, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, can I ask a question while it's still on to the witness. Mr. Witness, in this video, the prisoners, detainees, seem to have some kind of uniform. They are all wearing the same clothes, same hat. You notice that? Is that -- was that provided by the camp authorities, or is it just coincidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it's coincidence for this particular event, or as far as this event is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That means that they have been dressed like this for this particular event, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm so sorry, I think I did miss one document. Did I have 1591 in? I think I missed that by mistake. So I have missed it. Can I have up 1591. And Your Honours, could that not go on the screen and be marked under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I can't believe I missed this one either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You talked, sir, about the difference between Official Notes and reports. Is this an Official Note done by you in respect of the incident you earlier described from -- with the prisoners of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say, as you said in the beginning: "Compiled due to the violent and inhuman conduct of the Prijedor SJB employees towards the prisoners..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that, please, be admitted and marked under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P506 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just to go back for a moment, that really is the final question to the question that His Honour Judge Delvoie asked you, normally around the camp did the prisoners have uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: No, it was not usual. They went around in clothes in which they arrived. That's how it normally worked, but not always for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very much. Indeed, Your Honours, thank you for the latitude in allowing me more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is cross-examination by the Stanisic team declined, or you just decided to reverse the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just split the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. We've met before but for the record, my name is Dragan Krgovic. I am appearing for Mr. Stojan Zupljanin today. I have a few questions in regard of your evidence earlier today. Just let me remind you, we should avoid overlapping and in order to do that, before you start answering my question, make a pause of 15, 20 seconds to make it possible for the interpreters to interpret both the question and the answer. First I have a question regarding your last answer and a clarification that I believe was not recorded on the transcript. When you were asked by the Prosecutor about uniforms, you said they, meaning prisoners, wore clothes in which they arrived. That was what normally happened, but not with everyone, but you also said, at least I heard, that the prisoners wore the uniforms they arrived in, some of them had uniforms, there were uniforms available, but not for everyone. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot tell you in percentage how many were in uniform and how many in civilian clothing. There were both uniformed inmates and inmates in civilian clothing as they arrived to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move for a moment into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the Court and to the Prosecution because I've sent this document to translation services but I've only received back a partial translation. The whole document has about nine pages, but I'm only going to show the witness one passage. I'll ask the witness to read the document aloud so it can be interpreted so everyone can understand what it is about, and I believe that by the end of the day we'll have it in e-court, and obviously I'm not going to finish my cross-examination today, and tomorrow I'll come back to this document with some more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the private session, please, and this part must be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Please read this title.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-172
utterances.text: "Methods of combat training for military police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for page 2 of this document, Chapter 7. Page 175.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you earlier today which persons have the status of prisoners of war, and you gave a textbook narrow definition of prisoners of war. I will read out this definition here bit by bit and from your knowledge and experience, you will confirm to me whether all these categories of persons have indeed the status of prisoner of war. It says: "A prisoner of war is understood to be a person who has the following status --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, it's less than a minute before we take the adjournment. Is there any point in beginning this because you couldn't possibly finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour. Maybe I can finish -- a couple minutes before if you have two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, it's time now, as I say, because no two clocks have the same time, I always follow the clock in LiveNote. So perhaps you can pick this up tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I finish now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we are about to take the adjournment for today. We are obliged to break at 1.45 which is the time now. Having been sworn as a witness, I'm obliged to caution you that you cannot communicate with the lawyers from either side in this matter. Furthermore, in such conversations as you may have with anybody outside of the courtroom, you can't discuss the testimony you are giving. So you will return to this courtroom, I believe we are still in this courtroom, at 9.00 -- for 9.00 tomorrow morning, and according to our present schedule, your testimony should be concluded sometime tomorrow. So you are now excused as a witness but not released. So we take the adjournment to tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 22nd day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
